Chapter 3: Embracing Suffering—Finding Meaning in Pain and Weakness.
Suffering... it’s something every single one of us faces, isn’t it? Nobody invites it in, and yet, it finds its way into all our lives. For some, it shows up as illness or loss. For others, it’s that dull ache of disappointment, or the sting that comes when you feel misunderstood.
In the quiet halls of a convent, where days were shaped by prayer and simple work, suffering took on so many shapes. There were the obvious struggles—like constant fevers, deep exhaustion, and bodies that just wouldn’t heal. But then there were the hidden hurts: feeling left out, the battle to forgive, or trying to love someone who’s just plain hard to love.
At first, it’s natural to want to push suffering away—to see it as something that blocks happiness, or even holiness. But over time, a new way of seeing things begins to take root. What if suffering isn’t just something to get through? What if it could actually change us, even draw out more love from our hearts?
That shift doesn’t come easy. It calls for letting go—letting go of control, accepting what you can’t change, and daring to trust that maybe, just maybe, pain has a purpose.
There were days when the suffering felt like too much. A cough that wouldn’t quit, another night with no sleep, or the sting of being passed over. Those moments really tested patience and faith. It was tempting to complain, to look for sympathy. But little by little, the realization grew: suffering, when it’s met with love, can be offered up as a gift. It becomes a way to stand with others who are hurting, even if they never say a word about it.
One evening, after a particularly tough day, she found herself sitting alone in the chapel. Praying felt impossible. God felt far away. But in that heavy silence, something new took root. Suffering wasn’t a punishment. It was an invitation—to trust, to let go, to love without expecting anything back.
She realized that pain could actually make her more like the One she loved—someone who suffered, not out of duty, but out of love for others.
Now, this new perspective didn’t make all the pain disappear. There were still weak days, moments of doubt, and times when it all felt way too much. But alongside the struggle, there was this gentle peace—a quiet confidence that none of it was wasted. Every ache, every letdown, every hidden sacrifice became part of a much bigger story. A story about redemption. About a love that keeps going, even when things are hard.
Most people spend their lives trying to dodge pain, doing whatever they can to avoid getting hurt. But in this story, suffering turned out to be a teacher. It revealed just how deep love can go, and how powerful trust really is.
The real secret? Holiness isn’t about running away from pain. It’s about embracing it, with open hands, believing that even the darkest moments can be transformed by love.
